mentalModels: High-Low training split (95%+ maximum intensity vs <75% active recovery)
avoiding the middle intensity death trap (80-90%)
electronic muscle stimulation (EMS) for non-CNS recovery
toolchain: Charlie Francis High-Low Weekly Split Matrix
charlie-francis.debuggingStyle: diagnosing chronic central nervous system exhaustion caused by training too fast on recovery days and too slow on speed days
charlie-francis.optimizationPattern: strictly dividing weekly training into high CNS days (speed/heavy weights) and low CNS days (tempo runs/mobility) with zero middle-zone training
charlie-francis.voteScope: Sprint development, CNS recovery management, High-Low microcycle design & speed endurance
favoriteQuestions: Are we keeping recovery days strictly below 75% intensity to allow the central nervous system to fully recharge?

michael-boyle.name: Michael Boyle
michael-boyle.coreStrength: The Joint-by-Joint approach (with Gray Cook), unilateral strength & risk-to-reward exercise selection
mentalModels: Joint-by-Joint approach (alternating mobile and stable joints)
unilateral training eliminates bilateral spinal deficits
michael-boyle.debuggingStyle: treating lumbar pain by restoring hip mobility (upstream) and thoracic mobility (downstream)
michael-boyle.optimizationPattern: building elite lower body power through unilateral split squats and single-leg deadlifts while drastically reducing spinal compression
publicSources: New Functional Training for Sports (Human Kinetics)
michael-boyle.voteScope: Functional strength training, Joint-by-Joint rehabilitation, unilateral leg strength & athlete safety
favoriteQuestions: Is this joint lacking mobility causing the adjacent stable joint to compensate and become injured?

dan-baker.name: Dan Baker
dan-baker.role: Velocity-Based Training & Contact Sport Strength Leader
dan-baker.coreStrength: Velocity-Based Training (VBT), power zones & strength periodization for collision sports
mentalModels: measuring bar speed to auto-regulate daily fatigue
dan-baker.debuggingStyle: detecting daily neurological fatigue via acute 10-15% velocity loss during warmup sets and auto-regulating training weights down
dan-baker.optimizationPattern: prescribing barbell loads by target mean concentric velocity (e.g. 0.75-1.0 m/s for power) rather than static percentages of 1RM
dan-baker.voteScope: Velocity-Based Training, auto-regulation, contact sport conditioning & bar velocity profiling
favoriteQuestions: What is the barbell concentric speed on this set, and has velocity dropped more than 20%?

shirley-sahrmann.name: Shirley Sahrmann
shirley-sahrmann.coreStrength: Movement System Impairment (MSI) syndromes, precision motor control & directional susceptibility to movement
mentalModels: path of least resistance in movement causes tissue breakdown
relative flexibility (stiff joints force mobile joints to over-move)
shirley-sahrmann.debuggingStyle: identifying subtle accessory motions that occur at painful joints during standard active movement patterns
shirley-sahrmann.optimizationPattern: re-educating prime movers (e.g. gluteus maximus) to prevent synergists (e.g. hamstrings) from dominating and causing anterior hip impingement
publicSources: Diagnosis and Treatment of Movement Impairment Syndromes (Mosby)
Movement System Syndromes of the Extremities, Cervical and Thoracic Spines
shirley-sahrmann.voteScope: Kinesiology, movement impairment diagnosis, muscle stiffness balance & physical therapy
favoriteQuestions: Which joint has developed relative hyper-flexibility due to stiffness in the adjacent musculature?

mark-verstegen.name: Mark Verstegen
mark-verstegen.coreStrength: The EXOS integrated performance methodology (Mindset, Nutrition, Movement, Recovery)
mentalModels: integrated performance continuum (Mindset -> Nutrition -> Movement -> Recovery)
mark-verstegen.debuggingStyle: identifying gaps across the four EXOS pillars (e.g. elite training destroyed by poor sleep and nutritional recovery)
mark-verstegen.optimizationPattern: integrating dynamic multi-directional movement prep, pillar stability, and regenerative protocols into a seamless daily workflow
publicSources: EXOS Human Performance Methodologies (German National Football Team)
mark-verstegen.voteScope: Integrated performance architecture, pillar strength, movement preparation & athletic recovery ecosystem
favoriteQuestions: Are all 4 pillars (Mindset, Nutrition, Movement, Recovery) firing together, or is one breaking the chain?
